text: TERRIBLE / FINANCES / [green label: IM' BROKE!] / [red label: INSANE!]
scene: A cartoon heavyset man with auburn hair, a white short-sleeved shirt and blue trousers presses his left palm over one eye with his mouth pulled into a clenched-teeth grimace. At lower right two framed photo insets with thick black borders sit under the headline: on the left a young person with blond hair and black-rimmed glasses cries with an open mouth, on the right a woman with a wrinkled nose and wide-open mouth appears to shout. A curved black arrow sweeps from the end of FINANCES down toward the two insets.
mechanism: A cartoon facepalm plus two raw reaction-style photo clips stage the title's 'reacts to' format and cast the clips as examples of bad money behaviour.
composition: The cartoon man fills the left third from top to bottom and is the largest shape, while the headline owns the upper right and the two insets are pushed to the bottom edge, where they are cropped at the frame's lower edge. The arrow ties headline to insets, giving a clear left-to-right then downward path, and white space on the right of the insets is left empty.
typography: Two stacked heavy black lines, TERRIBLE and FINANCES, dominate; the two small labels above the insets are green and red and much smaller, with IM' BROKE! carrying a stray apostrophe in place of the missing letter. TERRIBLE FINANCES stays crisp at 160x90 but the two labels shrink to a few coloured pixels.
colors: Bright white ground, solid black headline, a skin-tone cartoon face and a white shirt. Saturated green and red label text and the black arrow are the only accents, so the labels pop against white but the two photo insets carry muted skin and dark-frame tones.
psychology: The cartoon man has a squeezed-shut eye, hand over brow and bared teeth; the inset faces have open mouths and one has visibly reddened eyes. These support a distress interpretation without establishing anger or embarrassment.
partnership: The title promises a reaction to twenty people, but the thumbnail shows only two clips and offers no count. TERRIBLE FINANCES supplies the verdict the title leaves implicit, and the two labels hint at contrasting reasons without saying what they are.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the facepalming cartoon face first, then TERRIBLE FINANCES, then the arrow down to the two crying and shouting insets, with the green and red labels last.
art: Flat digital cartoon with a thick outline and a clean white cutout, set against two photographic crops with a different lighting and texture, so the frame mixes illustration with screen-grab imagery. The stray apostrophe in IM' BROKE! and the labels' tight outlines show a quick overlay; the white background keeps clutter low.
strength: Three distinct pained faces and a bold two-word verdict make the emotional premise obvious at a glance.
weakness: The two small coloured labels and photo faces are too fine to read at phone size, and the number 20 from the title is absent.
bottleneck: The viewer cannot tell what the insets are or why these people count as financially illiterate, so the image reads as generic mockery.
action: Hypothesis: crop each inset to the face and enlarge the label to test whether legible reaction faces lift the small-size read.
mechanism_secondary: reaction clips as social proof of failure
counterexample: Seq 7 pairs one cartoon man with a single large figure and one prop, where this frame splits attention among a cartoon and two photos.
expression_label: hand over eye with grimace; crying; shouting
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: $87,400 / $85,000 [struck through in red] / STILL NOT ENOUGH [prop: Job Offer on the paper]
scene: A cartoon man with spiky dark-brown hair, a pale blank face, a navy suit and a blue tie sits at a wooden kitchen table and reads a sheet headed Job Offer. On the table sit a mug, a calculator, a second sheet and a few loose green banknotes. Behind him a rain-streaked window, a radiator, a fridge and a lit lamp or shelf with utensils at far right set a gloomy kitchen at night.
mechanism: A struck-through lower salary beside a higher one, over a grim kitchen scene, states that a raise has arrived and still fails to solve the money problem.
composition: The man sits right of centre and the headline fills the upper left, so the face and the number block balance diagonally. The table and the paper in his hand form a lower anchor; the window and the fridge fill the rest with dark mid-tones, which gives a dense but ordered frame.
typography: White heavy sans $87,400 over STILL NOT ENOUGH on two left-aligned lines, with $85,000 in red with a strike line beside the top number. The two big numbers and STILL NOT ENOUGH survive at 160x90; the Job Offer text on the paper does not.
colors: A dark teal-grey night kitchen with a warm amber glow at the right and bright white headline text. The only saturated element is the red struck-through $85,000, which reads as a correction mark rather than an alarm, and the man's navy suit blends into the dark table area.
psychology: Flat mouth, level brows and dot eyes angled down at the paper give a deflated, tired look, and the rain at the window and the dim light add a downbeat mood. Nothing signals panic; it reads as quiet disappointment.
partnership: The title says life gets easier at the right salary; the thumbnail answers with STILL NOT ENOUGH, which pushes against the title's promise and raises the question of what is eating the money. The specific figures add information the title lacks.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white $87,400 first, then the red struck-through figure beside it, then STILL NOT ENOUGH, then the man's flat face and the Job Offer paper.
art: Painterly cartoon with soft lighting, a blank pale face and detailed environment textures such as the radiator, tile and grain on the table. The man's face is deliberately empty and consistent; the scene is coherent, though the dim detail turns to mud at 160x90 while the headline stays clear.
strength: Two concrete salary numbers and a blunt verdict give the thumbnail a specific, tension-bearing claim.
weakness: The dark detailed kitchen competes with the headline and the Job Offer paper turns to an unreadable grey block at small size.
bottleneck: Which of the two numbers is the real salary, and why one is struck out, is unclear without the title, so the numbers can read as a confusing price edit.
action: Hypothesis: drop the struck-through $85,000 or label it and test whether a single salary number reads faster.
mechanism_secondary: specific numbers in a dark domestic scene
counterexample: Seq 24 also treats paycheck stress but on a bright white ground with an on-screen cartoon, where this frame uses a dark detailed scene.
expression_label: flat mouth and level brows, eyes down on paper
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SO YOU WANT TO / OWN A CINEMA / Building Acquisition & Construction Costs / Equipment & Technology Costs / Movie Licensing Costs / Staff & Operating Expenses / Revenue Streams / Marketing & Advertising Costs / Maintenance & Utilities / Financing & Interest Costs / Profitability & ROI [props: CINEMA marquee, NOW SHOWING, TICKETS, POP CORN, sign list TICKET SALES / FOOD & BEVERAGE / ON-SCREEN ADVERTISING / PRIVATE EVENTS & RENTALS / MERCHANDISE, poster words ACTION / ADVENTURE / SCI-FI / DRAMA]
scene: A symmetrical illustrated cinema with a red-lit CINEMA marquee, a NOW SHOWING sign, four posters, a red carpet with rope stanchions, a TICKETS booth at the left, a striped POP CORN bucket and red cup, and a green-bordered sign panel at the right listing five revenue lines. Nine hand-written labels in two rows, each with a small curved arrow, surround the building and name cost and revenue categories.
mechanism: A labelled infographic of the building turns the topic into a visible cost-and-revenue map, so the thumbnail itself promises a breakdown.
composition: A centred two-line headline sits on top, a red underline divides it from the building, and the building fills the lower two thirds with the marquee at the centre. Labels ring the building left, top and bottom in symmetric positions, giving an orderly diagram layout with no single person or object competing for the eye.
typography: SO YOU WANT TO sits above a much larger OWN A CINEMA in heavy black capitals; both lines are crisp at 160x90. The nine italic handwritten labels, the sign list and the poster words are thin and dissolve to hairline marks at that size, and the headline dominates over them.
colors: White ground with black headline and red underline, then the building's dark brown and red facade, a cream popcorn bucket, and a green-orange-brown sign panel. Red accents on the marquee, carpet and label underlines repeat across the frame, which unifies it, and no colour signals danger.
psychology: No face or person appears, so the frame relies on an invitation tone in the phrase SO YOU WANT TO and a tidy, textbook look. The cues are curiosity about cost categories and a sense of a complete guide, not emotion.
partnership: The headline restates the title's topic in a conversational tone, and the nine cost labels add a preview of what the video covers, including the unusual ROI and financing items. The risk is that listing every category in the image reveals the outline without raising a question.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: OWN A CINEMA first, then the glowing red CINEMA marquee, then the nearest labels around the building, with the right-hand revenue panel last.
art: Polished AI-style illustration with consistent lighting and a clean white cutout around the building and shrubs. The posters, marquee letters and sign panel are coherent and legible at full size; at 160x90 the fine labels and the roof detail merge into texture.
strength: The marquee-and-labels building turns an abstract economics topic into a concrete, instantly recognisable object.
weakness: Nine thin handwritten labels and a five-row sign panel are unreadable at 160x90, so the information density does not survive on mobile.
bottleneck: There is no emotional or numeric hook; the frame reads like a school diagram rather than a surprising claim.
action: Hypothesis: replace the nine labels with one headline-scale number, such as an operating-margin figure, to test whether a single stat beats the full diagram.
counterexample: Seq 10 has almost no information and one black background shape, where this frame packs a full diagram of labels.
hero_object: illustrated cinema building with cost labels
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with auburn hair, half-lidded eyes and a closed-mouth smirk wears a pale blue collared shirt, dark blue trousers and an orange belt buckle, and holds a stack of green banknotes in one outstretched hand. A small pile of green bills lies at his feet on a plank-striped floor, and a green vault door stands at the lower right, with a thick curved black arrow from the end of the headline pointing at it.
mechanism: Handing cash toward a vault, with an arrow at the safe, pictures saving money as the starting point of wealth.
composition: The man stands at the left with his head in the top half, the three-line headline fills the upper right, and the green vault sits at the lower right as the arrow's target. The cash in his hand and the pile at his feet lead the eye diagonally to the vault, and white space around the figure keeps the frame open.
typography: Three stacked lines of extra-bold black capitals, with REAL WEALTH the widest, run nearly the full width on the right. All three lines remain legible at 160x90; the headline is a statement of place and adds no figure, although the title carries $100K and $1 Million.
colors: White ground, black letters and outlines, a warm face, light blue shirt and dark blue trousers surround bright green cash and vault. Green links the money props but is not the only color.
psychology: Half-lidded eyes, a closed smile and an extended hand provide a relaxed visual cue. No fear expression or explicit urgency signal appears.
partnership: The title promises a path from $100K to $1 million and a hidden maths lesson; the thumbnail drops both numbers and offers only an abstract starting point. The question of where wealth starts is open, but the vault image gives away a fairly generic answer, saving.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the huge REAL WEALTH line first, then the man's face, then the cash in his hand, with the arrow leading down to the green vault last.
art: Flat cartoon with a thick outline and clean white cutout, though the safe is drawn as a green tube-like drum with perspective that does not match the man's front-on view. The faint plank lines of the floor add a ground plane without clutter.
strength: A single character, a stack of cash and a vault give a clean three-object story that survives at phone size.
weakness: The headline is a generic line without a number, so it drops the specific $100K to $1 Million promise the title carries.
bottleneck: The vault target tells only the generic answer saving, and the frame holds no tension or surprising claim.
action: Hypothesis: add the number 1M or 100K to the vault door to test whether a stated target improves the title-thumbnail link.
counterexample: Seq 7 also uses a cartoon man and a safe but puts a large dollar number in the headline, which this frame leaves out.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: An older woman with grey hair and a beige knit sweater lifts a cream mug to her mouth with one hand while a blood-pressure cuff is wrapped on her other forearm, and she looks at the monitor with furrowed brows and slightly open lips. The white monitor in the centre shows a red upward arrow and orange ascending bars, with a red-to-green colour strip at its left edge. At right a bearded man in glasses, a white coat and navy scrubs raises an open palm toward the viewer with furrowed brows, and a yellow arrow points from the headline area to the monitor.
mechanism: The coffee cup, the cuff and a screen with a rising red arrow tie a drink to a blood-pressure spike, while the raised doctor's palm adds a stop signal.
composition: The woman at the left, the monitor in the centre and the doctor at the right form three evenly spaced focal points, with the headline above the monitor between the two faces. The yellow arrow links the cup toward the screen, and both faces sit in the upper half at large scale.
typography: Four words over two lines: ONE CUP? in yellow with a dark outline above BP in white and UP? in white on a red rounded box. The red box and yellow type stay readable at 160x90, and the question marks leave both questions open; the title's 'and when it May be fine' half is missing.
colors: A dark navy and warm-brown background lets the yellow and white headline and the red box stand out; the monitor's red arrow echoes the red UP? box. Warm skin tones on the faces and the white coat give separation from the dark backdrop.
psychology: Her wide, worried stare at the monitor and the doctor's frowning brows with an outstretched stop-hand create concern and caution cues. The red rising arrow and red box raise alarm, hedged only by the two question marks.
partnership: The title balances when coffee can raise blood pressure and when it may be fine; the thumbnail asks only the warning half in two short questions. The red arrow answers 'yes' visually, so it leans more toward concern than the title does.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow ONE CUP? first, then the red UP? box, then the woman's stare and the monitor's red arrow, and finally the doctor's raised hand and face.
art: Photographic-style render with consistent warm lighting on the woman and cool lighting on the doctor; the monitor's screen and the cuff are coherent and sharp. The three-subject layout is busy but reads at 160x90 because the headline and the red arrow stay high contrast.
strength: A cup, a cuff, a rising arrow and a stop-hand tell the coffee-to-blood-pressure story in one glance.
weakness: Two faces, a monitor and a headline compete for the centre, and the red arrow suggests a spike more strongly than the hedged title does.
bottleneck: The image shows only the risky half of the title's balanced claim, so a viewer who sees the red arrow gets a fear message the title partly softens.
action: Hypothesis: add a small green check on the cup side of the monitor strip to test whether a balanced visual matches the title's 'may be fine' half.
counterexample: Seq 13 uses a similar doctor-and-prop layout but with a darker, calmer scene and no arrow, where this frame uses bright warning colours.
expression_label: worried stare; frowning with raised palm
hero_object: blood-pressure monitor with rising red arrow
medical_notes: Packaging judgement only: the red upward arrow and stop-palm lean toward the risk side of the title's two-sided coffee claim, while the question marks keep it hedged.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon older man with swept-back grey hair, round glasses and a grey beard wears a green and teal argyle sweater vest, a cream shirt and brown trousers, and clutches a burlap sack marked with a dollar sign in both hands. His eyes dart to the side, his brows are knitted and his teeth are clenched. A curved red arrow starts at the word ROTH and points back toward his lower legs.
mechanism: A man clutching a sack of money with a nervous sideways look pictures avoidance and fear of letting go of savings.
composition: The figure stands in the left quarter at full height with a thin vertical silhouette, and the three-line headline fills the right 60 percent. The red arrow connects the last word back to the man, but it points to his legs rather than the sack, and the headline outweighs the character.
typography: Three lines of tall condensed black capitals with wide letter-spacing, with AVOIDING slightly smaller than RETIREES and ROTH. All three words are crisp at 160x90, and ROTH is the key word placed last; the thumbnail drops the title's 'Why' and 'Conversion'.
colors: White ground with black type, an olive and teal sweater vest and brown trousers, and a single red arrow as the only saturated accent. The muted earthy tones keep the character calm, so the arrow is the only alarm cue.
psychology: Darting side-glance eyes, gritted teeth and a tight two-handed grip on the sack read as anxious guarding of money. The older man's age cues signal that the target audience is retirees.
partnership: The title asks why retirees avoid Roth conversion; the thumbnail restates 'retirees avoiding Roth' with nearly the same wording and no additional fact. The anxious-hoarder image supplies an emotional answer but leaves the actual reason unstated.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the large ROTH and RETIREES text first, then the anxious face of the man, then the money sack, with the red arrow last.
art: Clean cartoon with consistent ink outlines and flat fills; the sweater pattern and the hands on the sack are drawn coherently. The tall thin figure and white ground leave much unused space below the headline.
strength: The tight-grip sack and side-glance give a clear emotional metaphor for avoidance with only one character.
weakness: The headline repeats the title almost word for word, so the text carries no new information.
bottleneck: The red arrow points at the man's legs rather than the sack, so the arrow adds no clear meaning and the reason for avoidance is missing.
action: Hypothesis: aim the arrow at the dollar sack and add a one-word reason such as TAXES to test whether a stated reason increases specificity.
counterexample: Seq 20 also stars an older cartoon man but shows the debt cards in his hand and puts the key word on a red bar, where this frame has a sack and no highlighted keyword.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with auburn hair, half-lidded eyes looking sideways and a smirk wears a pale blue shirt with rolled sleeves and jeans, and bends forward to polish a small grey safe with a yellow cloth. The safe has a pale green door panel and a dial. A curved black arrow starts under the word RULE and sweeps down to the left toward the safe.
mechanism: Polishing a safe beneath a giant dollar figure suggests that a savings milestone is something to be guarded and maintained.
composition: The headline takes the right half and the figure with the safe the left half, the man's torso leaning inward toward the safe so that his gaze and the safe sit near the bottom. The $50,000 is the largest element, and the arrow forms a diagonal that returns the eye to the safe.
typography: Three lines with a huge black $50,000 between small THE above and RULE below; the digits are the heaviest element and read at once at 160x90. The text adds the number but the title's 'savings' and 'what changes' idea is missing.
colors: White ground, black type and outlines, soft skin tones and light blue shirt, and the safe's grey body with a mint-green face as the sole colour accent. The palette is quiet, so the black numeral dominates.
psychology: Sideways half-lidded eyes and a faint smirk read as relaxed pride while he wipes the safe. Nothing in the frame signals fear, which makes the number the only attention cue.
partnership: The title asks what changes at $50,000; the thumbnail turns it into a named rule and repeats the figure, so the number is duplicated while the word RULE adds a promised formula. It leaves open what the rule is.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the oversized $50,000 first, then the man's face, then the safe he polishes, with the arrow and RULE read last.
art: Flat cartoon with consistent outlines and a clean cutout on white; the hands and cloth are drawn coherently and the safe is simple. The commas inside $50,000 slightly touch the R of RULE below, a minor overlap that does not hurt reading.
strength: One giant number and one cherished object give an immediately readable, simple promise.
weakness: The man's polishing pose and the safe's meaning are ambiguous, so the visual does not explain what the rule is.
bottleneck: The word RULE promises a formula but the image contains no rule content, so the curiosity gap relies on the number alone.
action: Hypothesis: replace THE with a verb such as BREAK to test whether an action word creates more tension than a neutral article.
mechanism_secondary: named rule with a prized object
counterexample: Seq 4 uses the same character and vault but no number, so it lacks the specific figure this frame leads with.

scene: A yellow band across the top holds the headline over two side-by-side panels. In the left panel a headless torso in a black T-shirt on a teal ground wears a glowing red colon overlay with a lumpy brown mass in the upper bowel, and both hands rest on the lower abdomen. In the right panel a bare midsection with hands on hips carries a red overlay of a Y-shaped arrow pointing down the centre and an oval loop of arrows with small black arrowheads circling the navel.
mechanism: A glowing blocked colon beside a red arrow map on a bare belly pairs the problem with a how-to massage direction, so the image states the method as well as the issue.
composition: The yellow headline runs the full width above a clean vertical split, with the colon overlay left and the arrow overlay right at similar scale. Both torsos are cropped at the neck and thighs, so the arrows and colon are the only focal shapes, and the layout is symmetrical and uncluttered.
typography: Three heavy black capitals on a solid yellow band span the full width, so each word stays readable at 160x90. The headline names the symptom and the method but omits the title's '5 KG' and 'flushes out' claim.
colors: Black headline on saturated yellow, a teal left backdrop, black shirt and bright red overlays. The yellow-black pairing reads like a caution band, and the red glow and arrows add a second alert tone against the pale skin on the right.
psychology: No face is visible, so the cues are the glowing red colon with a brown mass and the dense arrows, which suggest a blockage and urgency. The viewer is addressed through the body shown rather than a person.
partnership: The title adds a bold outcome claim, flushing out 5 KG of stuck stool, that the thumbnail does not repeat; the thumbnail instead shows the blockage and the massage path. The two together promise relief, and the image does not contradict the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow CONSTIPATION COLON MASSAGE band first, then the red glowing colon with its brown mass, then the red arrow loop on the right belly.
art: Mixed media of photographic torsos with a stylised red anatomy overlay; the colon's rectum hangs as a long tail down past the hands and the brown mass is rendered in glossy detail, so the anatomy is schematic rather than realistic. The arrow overlay on the right is flat and mismatched with the skin lighting.
strength: A split layout shows the problem on one side and the method on the other, with a headline that survives at phone size.
weakness: The stylised, oversized stool image is a graphic medical depiction that may read as exaggerated, and the arrow loop on the right is dense.
bottleneck: Both panels are body close-ups with no person or face, so the frame has no human cue and the stool visual is the main attention driver.
action: Hypothesis: replace the brown mass with a plain blockage marker to test whether a less graphic cue keeps the click-worthy premise.
mechanism_secondary: before-the-fix anatomy with a massage path
counterexample: Seq 22 pairs a body part with a number reading, where this frame uses an anatomical overlay with no numbers.
hero_object: glowing red colon with stool mass
medical_notes: Packaging judgement only: the title's flush-out-5-KG claim and the glossy stool-in-colon graphic overstate what a belly massage can do, though the thumbnail alone only shows the problem and a massage path.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with spiky dark hair streaked purple, tan skin, a raised eyebrow, side-glancing half-lidded eyes and a closed smile wears a pink polo shirt and points one index finger toward the lower right. At the lower right stands a grey two-storey house with a blue roof and chimney, wrapped by a thick red chain around its walls and base on a strip of green grass. A curved black arrow starts beneath WHO? and sweeps down-left toward the house.
mechanism: A man pointing toward a chained house under the question WHO? pictures a $500K home as something locked away from most buyers.
composition: The man's large head takes the left 40 percent and his pointing finger crosses into the centre to link him to the house. The two-line headline sits above the house at the upper right and the arrow runs from the headline to the roof, so the face, finger, house and text read as one continuous loop with white space around the house.
typography: Two lines of black capitals: a smaller $500K... with a trailing ellipsis above a much bigger WHO?, both readable at 160x90. The ellipsis and the question mark add a leading question that the title answers only partly; the title's 2026 and 'The Math Is Brutal' do not appear.
colors: White ground and black type contrast with tan skin, pink shirt, blue roof and gray house siding. Saturated red chain links emphasize a barrier around the house; other colored elements remain visible.
psychology: The lifted eyebrow, sideways glance and shut-mouth smile with a pointing finger read as a knowing, teasing prompt to the viewer. The red chain adds a constraint or burden cue without any fear expression.
partnership: The title asks who can actually afford a $500K house and says the math is brutal; the thumbnail turns the figure into a short question and the chain adds the sense of being trapped. The thumbnail does not answer who can, so the curiosity gap stays open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the oversized WHO? first, then the man's teasing face and pointing finger, then the chained house, with the arrow confirming the target.
art: Smooth cartoon with consistent outlines, a clean cutout and a plain white ground. The finger, chain links and house windows are drawn coherently, and the chain wraps the house convincingly even at a small size.
strength: A pointing character, a chained house and a one-word question explain the unaffordability idea with very few elements.
weakness: The cartoon's relaxed smile does not match the title's 'brutal' tone, so the mood is playful where the title is grim.
bottleneck: Nothing shows who the answer might be or what income is needed, so the question stays abstract until the video.
action: Hypothesis: add a salary figure beside the chain to test whether a concrete income number sharpens the curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 24 uses a similar character plus an arrow but treats the money problem as a paycheck mirage with several props, where this frame has one prop.

evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A black frame holds a thick white winding shaft that drops from the top centre, bends left, then right, and ends near the lower middle. At its bottom a tiny hand-drawn stick figure with a round head swings a pick, and a trail of dark specks flies up from the pick. A red circle at the lower left carries a black silhouette of a dinosaur hanging in a rope sling above the white lowercase words what if?
mechanism: A bottomless white tunnel with a tiny digger at its end shows the title's endless digging as a single stark shape.
composition: The white shaft cuts the black frame vertically near the middle, and the stick figure at its lower end is the smallest element, which gives a strong sense of depth and scale. The red logo disc anchors the lower-left corner, and everything else is black negative space.
typography: The only text is the lowercase what if? inside the red disc at the lower left, which stays readable at 160x90 as a series mark. The thumbnail carries no headline, so the title's digging question appears nowhere in the image.
colors: Pure black background and a white shaft produce maximum two-tone contrast, with a red disc and white lettering as the single accent. The palette is minimal and has no mid-tones.
psychology: No expression is visible; the stick figure's head is a plain circle. The cues are scale contrast and darkness, which suggest depth and isolation.
partnership: The title asks what if you kept digging downward and the image shows a figure digging down a long shaft, so the picture illustrates the title directly but adds no number, depth or consequence. The mystery of the bottom is carried by the dark negative space.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white winding shaft first, then the red what if? disc, then the tiny stick figure at the bottom of the shaft.
art: Hand-drawn minimal vector shapes with a rough-edged white tunnel and a few speck marks, in the series' stick-figure style. The shaft's wavy outline is deliberate and the stick figure is only a few pixels wide at small size.
strength: The stark white-on-black tunnel is unlike anything else in the batch and creates a clear sense of depth.
weakness: The stick figure and pick are tiny and the image has no headline, so the frame depends on the title for meaning.
bottleneck: At 160x90 the digger vanishes and the white shape reads as an abstract worm or crack, so the digging story is lost.
action: Hypothesis: add a depth number such as 6,000 km next to the shaft to test whether a stated scale gives the shape a clear meaning.
mechanism_secondary: extreme scale contrast in a minimal drawing
counterexample: Seq 3 packs a full labelled diagram into the frame, where this one holds a single white shape.

scene: A giant black GERMANY spans the top while five cartoon characters stand shoulder to shoulder below it. From the left: a pale soldier in a dark green helmet and olive uniform with red-rimmed streaming eyes and a toothy grin; a bearded man in a red knit beanie with drooping lids and a cigarette in his mouth, glancing aside; a blonde woman with braids, blue eyes and red lips in a low white top who holds two full beer steins in the foreground; a figure in a yellow hooded raincoat with bulging eyes and a gaping mouth; and a pale woman with long black hair, a black choker ring, a cross mark on her cheek and facial piercings.
mechanism: One country name above a lineup of exaggerated archetypes sets up a stereotype gallery, so the image itself is the list the title promises.
composition: The headline fills the top 40 percent, and the five characters form a tight row across the bottom with the blonde woman centred and slightly larger, creating a symmetrical lineup. Overlapping bodies and the beer steins in front crowd the lower band, so the face row is the second focal zone below the text.
